claim: The gut microbiota of the Western honey bee (Apis mellifera) is composed of a few deep-branching phylogenetic lineages (phylotypes) belonging to the Firmicutes, Actinobacteria, and Proteobacteria phyla.
source: The gut microbiota of the Western honey bee (Apis mellifera) is composed of a few deep-branching phylogenetic lineages (phylotypes) belonging to the Firmicutes, Actinobacteria, and Proteobacteria phyla (Martinson et al., 2011; Kwong and Moran, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Martinson et al., 2011; Kwong and Moran, 2016).

claim: Most phylogenetic lineages of the honey bee gut microbiota are composed of several closely related sequence-discrete populations (species), each containing further diversity at the strain-level.
source: Most of these lineages are composed of several closely related sequence-discrete populations, hereafter referred to as species, each of which contains further diversity at the strain-level (Ellegaard and Engel, 2016; Ellegaard and Engel, 2019; Engel et al., 2012; Ellegaard et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Ellegaard and Engel, 2016; Ellegaard and Engel, 2019; Engel et al., 2012; Ellegaard et al., 2015).

claim: Microbiota-depleted bees can be generated and experimentally colonized with synthetic communities of different strains.
source: Microbiota-depleted bees can be generated and experimentally colonized with synthetic communities of different strains.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about experimental methods with honey bees.

claim: Most community members of the honey bee gut microbiota can be cultured in pollen, which is the major dietary source of honey bees.
source: Moreover, most community members can be cultured in pollen, which is the major dietary source of honey bees (Kešnerová et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research (Kešnerová et al., 2017).

claim: Lactobacillus Firm5 is one of the most abundant and diverse phylotypes of the honey bee gut microbiota.
source: One of the most abundant and diverse phylotype of the honey bee gut microbiota is Lactobacillus Firm5 (Ellegaard and Engel, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research (Ellegaard and Engel, 2019).

claim: Lactobacillus Firm5 consists of facultative anaerobes that ferment sugars into organic acids.
source: This phylotype consists of facultative anaerobes that ferment sugars into organic acids and utilize various pollen-derived glycosylated plant compounds, such as flavonoids (Kešnerová et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research (Kešnerová et al., 2017).

claim: Lactobacillus Firm5 utilizes various pollen-derived glycosylated plant compounds, such as flavonoids.
source: This phylotype consists of facultative anaerobes that ferment sugars into organic acids and utilize various pollen-derived glycosylated plant compounds, such as flavonoids (Kešnerová et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research (Kešnerová et al., 2017).

claim: Lactobacillus Firm5 is specific to social bees but has diverged into many different species.
source: Lactobacillus Firm5 is specific to social bees but has diverged into many different species of which four are specifically associated with the Western honey bee, Apis mellifera: Lactobacillus apis (Lapi), Lactobacillus helsingborgensis (Lhel), Lactobacillus melliventris (Lmel), and Lactobacillus kullabergensis (Lkul).
evidence: This claim is stated directly in the manuscript text.

claim: Four Lactobacillus Firm5 species are specifically associated with the Western honey bee: Lactobacillus apis (Lapi), Lactobacillus helsingborgensis (Lhel), Lactobacillus melliventris (Lmel), and Lactobacillus kullabergensis (Lkul).
source: Lactobacillus Firm5 is specific to social bees but has diverged into many different species of which four are specifically associated with the Western honey bee, Apis mellifera: Lactobacillus apis (Lapi), Lactobacillus helsingborgensis (Lhel), Lactobacillus melliventris (Lmel), and Lactobacillus kullabergensis (Lkul).
evidence: This claim is stated directly in the manuscript text.

claim: The four Lactobacillus Firm5 species are consistently present in the gut of individual honey bees.
source: The four species are consistently present in the gut of individual honey bees suggesting that they can share the available niches and stably coexist despite their phylogenetic relatedness.
evidence: This claim is stated directly in the manuscript text and suggests an observation from the field.

claim: The four Lactobacillus Firm5 species share <85% pairwise average nucleotide identities (gANI).
source: Genomic analysis has revealed that these species share <85% pairwise average nucleotide identities (gANI) and exhibit high levels of genomic variation in terms of carbohydrate metabolism (Ellegaard and Engel, 2019; Ellegaard et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Ellegaard and Engel, 2019; Ellegaard et al., 2015).

claim: The four Lactobacillus Firm5 species exhibit high levels of genomic variation in terms of carbohydrate metabolism.
source: Genomic analysis has revealed that these species share <85% pairwise average nucleotide identities (gANI) and exhibit high levels of genomic variation in terms of carbohydrate metabolism (Ellegaard and Engel, 2019; Ellegaard et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Ellegaard and Engel, 2019; Ellegaard et al., 2015).

claim: When mono-colonized, the four Lactobacillus species established in the gut of microbiota-depleted bees independent of the dietary treatment.
source: When mono-colonized, the four species established in the gut of microbiota-depleted bees independent of the dietary treatment (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In the sugar water treatment, colonization levels were generally lower than in the sugar water plus pollen treatment.
source: In the SW treatment, the colonization levels were generally lower than in the SW+PG treatment (Figure 1A, ANOVA q-value < 0.01) confirming previous results that pollen increases the total bacterial load in the gut (Kešnerová et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A with statistical analysis (ANOVA q-value < 0.01) and confirmed by citation (Kešnerová et al., 2020).

claim: Pollen increases the total bacterial load in the honey bee gut.
source: In the SW treatment, the colonization levels were generally lower than in the SW+PG treatment (Figure 1A, ANOVA q-value < 0.01) confirming previous results that pollen increases the total bacterial load in the gut (Kešnerová et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 1A and confirmed by citation (Kešnerová et al., 2020).

claim: The sum of the bacterial loads of the mono-colonizations exceeded the total bacterial load of the co-colonizations in both dietary treatments.
source: Consequently, the sum of the bacterial loads of the mono-colonizations exceeded the total bacterial load of the co-colonizations in both dietary treatments, suggesting that the species engage in negative interactions when colonizing the honey bee gut together.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data comparing mono-colonizations and co-colonizations.

claim: The four Lactobacillus species engage in negative interactions when colonizing the honey bee gut together.
source: Consequently, the sum of the bacterial loads of the mono-colonizations exceeded the total bacterial load of the co-colonizations in both dietary treatments, suggesting that the species engage in negative interactions when colonizing the honey bee gut together.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that total bacterial loads in co-colonizations are lower than the sum of mono-colonizations.

claim: In the sugar water treatment, three species (Lapi, Lmel and Lkul) steadily decreased in abundance across serial passages resulting in rapid dominance of Lhel.
source: However, three species (Lapi, Lmel and Lkul) steadily decreased in abundance in the subsequent passages resulting in a rapid dominance of Lhel (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B from serial passage experiments.

claim: In the sugar water plus pollen treatment, all four species were detectable in all passages at around 10^6 to 10^8 bacteria/gut and displayed a highly stable abundance profile over time.
source: In the contrary, in the SW+PG treatment, all four species were detectable in all passages at around 106 to 108 bacteria/gut, and displayed a highly stable abundance profile over time (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C from serial passage experiments.

claim: The four Lactobacillus species can stably coexist in vivo when bees are fed pollen, but not when they are only fed sugar water.
source: In summary, these findings show that the four species can stably coexist in vivo when bees are fed pollen, but not when they are only fed sugar water.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the serial passage experiments shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: Pollen facilitates niche partitioning in the honey bee gut by offering competing species different ecological niches facilitating their coexistence.
source: This is consistent with the idea that pollen facilitates niche partitioning in the honey bee gut by offering competing species different ecological niches facilitating their coexistence.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing stable coexistence in the presence of pollen but not sugar water.

claim: All four Lactobacillus species were able to grow when cultured alone in minimal medium supplemented with either glucose, pollen extract, or entire pollen grains.
source: All four species were able to grow when cultured alone under the three nutrient conditions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the presence of glucose during in vitro serial passage, Lapi was stably maintained at high abundance until the last passage and dominated the co-culture for most of the transfer experiment.
source: In contrast, Lapi was stably maintained at high abundance (109 bacteria/ml) until the last passage (Figure 2A) and hence dominated the co-culture for most of the transfer experiment.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A from in vitro serial passage experiments.

claim: In the presence of pollen extract or pollen grains during in vitro serial passage, none of the four species decreased over time, and after 21 transfers all species still yielded between 10^6 and 10^9 bacteria/ml.
source: In the presence of PE or PG, the four species revealed very different growth behaviors (Figure 2B and C). None of the species decreased over time, and after 21 transfers all species still yielded between 106 and 109 bacteria/ml.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2B and 2C from in vitro serial passage experiments.

claim: The nutrient-dependent coexistence of the four Lactobacillus species observed in vivo can be recapitulated in vitro in a simple co-culture experiment.
source: In summary, these findings show that the nutrient-dependent coexistence of the four Lactobacillus species observed in vivo can be recapitulated in vitro in a simple co-culture experiment, suggesting that the partitioning of pollen-derived nutrients is sufficient for enabling coexistence.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from both in vivo and in vitro serial passage experiments showing similar patterns.

claim: The partitioning of pollen-derived nutrients is sufficient for enabling coexistence of the four Lactobacillus species.
source: In summary, these findings show that the nutrient-dependent coexistence of the four Lactobacillus species observed in vivo can be recapitulated in vitro in a simple co-culture experiment, suggesting that the partitioning of pollen-derived nutrients is sufficient for enabling coexistence.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that coexistence can be recapitulated in vitro with pollen nutrients alone.

claim: A total of 687 genes (181 to 217 genes per species) were differentially expressed between the sugar water and sugar water plus pollen dietary treatments.
source: We found a total 687 genes (181 to 217 genes per species) to be differentially expressed (log2FC ≥ |2| and p-value ≤ 0.01) between the two dietary treatments (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: 'Carbohydrate transport and metabolism' (COG G) was by far the most abundant functional category among the genes upregulated in the sugar water plus pollen treatment relative to the sugar water treatment.
source: 'Carbohydrate transport and metabolism' (Cluster of orthologous group category G, COG G) was by far the most abundant functional category among the genes upregulated in the SW+PG treatment relative to the SW treatment (Figure 3C, 17.1–37.6% of all upregulated genes).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and functional annotation analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In three of the four species (Lmel, Lhel, and Lkul), the 'Carbohydrate transport and metabolism' category was significantly enriched among the upregulated genes.
source: In three of the four species (Lmel, Lhel, and Lkul), this category was significantly enriched among the upregulated genes (Fisher's exact test, p<0.01, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis (Fisher's exact test, p<0.01) of RNA sequencing data.

claim: The largest fraction of the upregulated COG G genes encoded PTS transporters.
source: The largest fraction of the upregulated COG G genes encoded PTS transporters (Figure 3D, Supplementary file 5), followed by other sugar transporters (e.g. ABC transporters), and enzymes involved in sugar cleavage and conversion (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and functional annotation analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The category 'Amino acid metabolism and transport' (COG E) was enriched among downregulated genes in Lapi.
source: Instead, the category 'Amino acid metabolism and transport' (COG E) was enriched in Lapi (Fisher's exact test, p < 0.01, Supplementary file 8), and genes encoding ABC-type amino acid transporters were present among the downregulated genes in all species (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis (Fisher's exact test, p < 0.01) of RNA sequencing data.

claim: While most of the differentially expressed genes belonged to gene families with homologs in multiple species, differential expression was typically observed for just one of the species.
source: While most of the differentially expressed genes (89%) belonged to gene families with homologs in multiple species, differential expression was typically observed for just one of the species (Figure 3E–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and gene family analysis shown in Figures 3E-F.

claim: The presence of pollen triggers distinct transcriptional changes in the four species during gut colonization.
source: This suggests that the presence of pollen triggers distinct transcriptional changes in the four species during gut colonization.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that differential expression was typically species-specific despite gene homology.

claim: Lhel specifically upregulated three PTS gene clusters for the uptake and metabolism of sugar alcohols and one gene cluster for ribose utilization.
source: For example, Lhel specifically upregulated three PTS gene clusters for the uptake and metabolism of sugar alcohols and one gene cluster for ribose utilization.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and gene annotation analysis.

claim: Lmel upregulated several gene clusters involved in the cleavage of xylose, mannose, rhamnose, and arabinose from polysaccharides or other glycosylated compounds.
source: In contrast, Lmel upregulated several gene clusters involved in the cleavage of xylose, mannose, rhamnose, and arabinose from polysaccharides or other glycosylated compounds.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and gene annotation analysis.

claim: Lmel upregulated a gene cluster for the synthesis and the transport of bacteriocins in the presence of pollen.
source: Lmel also upregulated a gene cluster for the synthesis and the transport of bacteriocins in the presence of pollen.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and gene annotation analysis.

claim: Lkul upregulated a starch utilization gene cluster, which in part was also differentially regulated in Lmel.
source: Lkul upregulated a starch utilization gene cluster, which in part was also differentially regulated in Lmel.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and gene annotation analysis.

claim: Lkul upregulated an oligopeptide transporter gene cluster that was present in some of the other strains but not differentially regulated.
source: In addition, this species upregulated an oligopeptide transporter gene cluster that was present in some of the other strains but not differentially regulated.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and gene annotation analysis.

claim: Lapi was the only species that upregulated two conserved deoxycytidine kinase genes encoding enzymes involved in nucleoside salvage pathways.
source: However, Lapi was the only species that upregulated two conserved deoxycytidine kinase genes encoding enzymes involved in nucleoside salvage pathways.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and gene annotation analysis.

claim: Lhel and Lkul upregulated genes encoding a citrate lyase for the conversion of citrate into oxaloacetate and acetate in the presence of pollen.
source: For example, we found evidence for citrate fermentation in Lhel and Lkul. Both species upregulated genes encoding a citrate lyase for the conversion of citrate into oxaloacetate and acetate in the presence of pollen (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and gene annotation analysis.

claim: Lhel, Lmel, and Lkul upregulated genes for the uptake and metabolism of glycerol.
source: Lhel, Lmel, and Lkul upregulated genes for the uptake and metabolism of glycerol.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and gene annotation analysis.

claim: All four species upregulated gene clusters encoding surface proteins with leucine-rich repeat (LRR) regions, LPXT cell-wall anchoring motifs, and SLAP (S-layer associated protein) domains.
source: Moreover, all four species upregulated gene clusters encoding surface proteins with leucine-rich repeat (LRR) regions, LPXT cell-wall anchoring motifs, and SLAP (S-layer associated protein) domains (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and gene annotation analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The four species utilize different carbohydrate-related resources from pollen, which supports the niche partitioning hypothesis as the basis for coexistence.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that the four species utilize different carbohydrate-related resources from pollen, which supports the niche partitioning hypothesis as the basis for coexistence.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the RNA sequencing data showing species-specific upregulation of different carbohydrate metabolism genes.

claim: For each species, whether grown alone or in co-culture, between 159 and 393 genes were differentially regulated between the pollen extract and glucose treatment.
source: For each species, whether grown alone or in co-culture, we found between 159 and 393 genes to be differentially regulated between the PE and the G treatment (Figure 5B, log2FC ≥ |2| and p-value≤0.01).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Carbohydrate transport and metabolism (COG 'G') was the predominant functional category among the upregulated genes in the presence of pollen in vitro.
source: As in vivo, Carbohydrate transport and metabolism (COG 'G') was the predominant functional category among the upregulated genes in the presence of pollen (Figure 5C) and enriched in all eight comparisons (four species, each alone or in co-culture, Fisher's exact test p-value < 0.01, Supplementary file 8).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and statistical analysis (Fisher's exact test p-value < 0.01) shown in Figure 5C.

claim: 25.3–36.9% of the genes upregulated in vivo were also upregulated in vitro in the presence of pollen.
source: Moreover, 25.3–36.9% of the genes upregulated in vivo were also upregulated in vitro in the presence of pollen.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of RNA sequencing data from in vivo and in vitro experiments.

claim: The species-specific carbohydrate metabolism functions showed a similar transcriptional response to pollen in vivo and in vitro.
source: In particular, the species-specific carbohydrate metabolism functions described above (Figure 4) showed a similar transcriptional response to pollen in vivo and in vitro (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of RNA sequencing data from in vivo and in vitro experiments shown in Figures 4 and 5D.

claim: Most of the putative adhesin genes upregulated in vivo were not upregulated in vitro during growth in pollen or had relatively low transcripts per million.
source: In contrast, most of the putative adhesin genes upregulated in vivo were not upregulated in vitro during growth in pollen or had relatively low transcripts per million (TPM).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of RNA sequencing data from in vivo and in vitro experiments.

claim: Each species upregulates specific operons for the transport and utilization of different carbohydrates in response to the presence of pollen, independent of the host environment.
source: Based on these results, we conclude that each species upregulates specific operons for the transport and utilization of different carbohydrates (e.g. sugar alcohols and glycans) in response to the presence of pollen, independent of the host environment.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of in vivo and in vitro RNA sequencing data showing similar patterns.

claim: A large fraction of the genes upregulated in pollen extract relative to glucose in the mono-cultures were also upregulated in the co-cultures (58.2–87.8%).
source: We found that a large fraction of the genes upregulated in PE relative to G in the mono-cultures were also upregulated in the co-cultures (58.2–87.8%, Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data comparing mono-cultures and co-cultures shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Fewer genes (9–149 genes) were differentially expressed between co-culture and mono-culture treatments compared to the nutritional treatments.
source: In comparison to the nutritional treatments, fewer genes (9–149 genes) were differentially expressed between co-culture and mono-culture treatments (log2FC ≥ |2| and p-value≤0.01), (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The main factor driving changes in gene expression in the four strains is the presence of pollen, rather than the presence of other Lactobacillus species.
source: We thus conclude that the main factor driving changes in gene expression in the four strains is the presence of pollen, rather than the presence of other Lactobacillus species.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of gene expression changes between nutritional treatments versus co-culture/mono-culture treatments.

claim: A total of 76 pollen-derived ions showed a significant decrease in abundance over-time (log2FC ≤ −1 and p-value≤0.01).
source: A total of 76 pollen-derived ions showed a significant decrease in abundance over-time (log2FC ≤ −1 and p-value≤0.01, Student's t-Test, BH correction) (Figure 6A, Supplementary file 10).
evidence: This claim is supported by metabolomics data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Lmel depleted six different ions annotated as flavonoids (isoorientin 2''-O-rhamnoside, quercetin-3-O-glucoside, vitexin, rutin, luteolin-7-O-(6''-malonylglucoside), and quercetin-3-O-beta-D-glucosyl-(1->2)-beta-D-glucoside).
source: Lmel depleted six different ions annotated as flavonoids (isoorientin 2''-O-rhamnoside, quercetin-3-O-glucoside, vitexin, rutin, luteolin-7-O-(6''-malonylglucoside), and quercetin-3-O-beta-D-glucosyl-(1->2)-beta-D-glucoside), while Lapi depleted three ions annotated as flavonoids (isoorientin 2''-O-rhamnoside, quercetin-3-O-glucoside, vitexin) (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Lapi depleted three ions annotated as flavonoids (isoorientin 2''-O-rhamnoside, quercetin-3-O-glucoside, vitexin).
source: Lmel depleted six different ions annotated as flavonoids (isoorientin 2''-O-rhamnoside, quercetin-3-O-glucoside, vitexin, rutin, luteolin-7-O-(6''-malonylglucoside), and quercetin-3-O-beta-D-glucosyl-(1->2)-beta-D-glucoside), while Lapi depleted three ions annotated as flavonoids (isoorientin 2''-O-rhamnoside, quercetin-3-O-glucoside, vitexin) (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Lkul only depleted the flavonoid ion annotated as isoorientin 2''-O-rhamnoside.
source: In contrast, Lkul only depleted the flavonoid ion annotated as isoorientin 2''-O-rhamnoside, and no flavonoid ion changes were identified for Lhel (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: No flavonoid ion changes were identified for Lhel.
source: In contrast, Lkul only depleted the flavonoid ion annotated as isoorientin 2''-O-rhamnoside, and no flavonoid ion changes were identified for Lhel (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Rutin was depleted in wells incubated with Lmel and a yellow precipitate corresponding to quercetin accumulated.
source: Metabolomics analysis confirmed that rutin was depleted in these wells and that the yellow precipitate corresponded to an accumulation of quercetin, the water-insoluble, deglycosylated aglycone of rutin (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by metabolomics data and visual observation shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Lmel is the only species that upregulated a rhamnosidase gene known to cleave rhamnose residue from rutin.
source: These findings are consistent with our transcriptome results which show that Lmel is the only species that upregulated a rhamnosidase gene known to cleave rhamnose residue from rutin (Beekwilder et al., 2009; Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4 and confirmed by citation (Beekwilder et al., 2009).

claim: Lhel was the only species depleting an ion corresponding to sugar alcohols (mannitol, D-sorbitol, or L-glucitol).
source: Lhel was the only species depleting an ion corresponding to sugar alcohols (mannitol, D-sorbitol, or L-glucitol) (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 3) consistent with the specific upregulation of sugar alcohol PTS transporters in this species (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 3, consistent with RNA sequencing data in Figure 4.

claim: The four species target different metabolites, in particular secondary plant metabolites present in pollen.
source: Based on the untargeted metabolomics analysis, we conclude that the four species target different metabolites, in particular secondary plant metabolites present in pollen.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the metabolomics data showing species-specific depletion of different pollen-derived compounds.

claim: All four species showed mixed substrate utilization, utilizing several substrates simultaneously.
source: All four species showed mixed substrate utilization, that is they utilized several substrates simultaneously.
evidence: This claim is supported by GC-MS metabolomics data.

claim: Most substrates were utilized by all four species, but often at different rates.
source: Moreover, most substrates were utilized by all four species, but often at different rates.
evidence: This claim is supported by GC-MS metabolomics data.

claim: All four species consumed the carboxylic acids citrate and malate.
source: Moreover, all four species consumed the carboxylic acids citrate and malate (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 4), which corresponded with the results of the Q-TOF-based experiment.
evidence: This claim is supported by GC-MS metabolomics data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: Lkul and Lhel consumed citrate at the fastest rate.
source: Interestingly, Lkul and Lhel consumed citrate at the fastest rate and they were also the two species that upregulated gene clusters for citrate fermentation in the presence of pollen in vivo and in vitro (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by GC-MS metabolomics data and is consistent with RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Lmel consumed several simple monosaccharides (such as glucose, fructose, allose, and mannose) at a slower rate than the other species.
source: Lmel consumed several simple monosaccharides (such as glucose, fructose, allose, and mannose) at a slower rate than the other species, although having a similar growth profile (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplements 4–5).
evidence: This claim is supported by GC-MS metabolomics data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplements 4–5.

claim: Lmel has specialized in the metabolism of pollen-derived glycosylated compounds at the expense of fast consumption of generic substrates.
source: This could indicate that Lmel has specialized in the metabolism of pollen-derived glycosylated compounds (such as rutin, Figure 6B–C) at the expense of fast consumption of generic substrates, which accords with the upregulation of several gene clusters for the cleavage of such sugars from polysaccharides or other glycosides (e.g. flavonoids) in presence of pollen (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is inferred from metabolomics data showing slower consumption of simple sugars and RNA sequencing data showing upregulation of glycoside cleavage genes.

claim: The four species specialize in the utilization of different pollen-derived compounds.
source: In summary, our metabolomics results show that the four species specialize in the utilization of different pollen-derived compounds, and that the observed metabolite changes are to some extent consistent with the transcriptional changes observed in the presence of pollen relative to the presence of simple sugars.
evidence: This claim is supported by metabolomics data showing species-specific depletion of different pollen-derived compounds.

claim: The observed metabolite changes are to some extent consistent with the transcriptional changes observed in the presence of pollen relative to the presence of simple sugars.
source: In summary, our metabolomics results show that the four species specialize in the utilization of different pollen-derived compounds, and that the observed metabolite changes are to some extent consistent with the transcriptional changes observed in the presence of pollen relative to the presence of simple sugars.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of metabolomics and transcriptomics data.

claim: The dynamics in the four-species community is governed by negative interactions.
source: We disentangled the effect of the diet and the host on the interactions between the four species by serially passaging them through gnotobiotic bees or in culture tubes, under two nutrient conditions (pollen versus simple sugars). Our results show that the dynamics in the four-species community is governed by negative interactions, because the growth of each member was lower in co-culture than in mono-culture, independent of the environment (host or culture tube) and the nutrient condition (pollen or simple sugars).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from serial passage experiments showing lower growth in co-culture than mono-culture.

claim: The growth of each member was lower in co-culture than in mono-culture, independent of the environment and the nutrient condition.
source: Our results show that the dynamics in the four-species community is governed by negative interactions, because the growth of each member was lower in co-culture than in mono-culture, independent of the environment (host or culture tube) and the nutrient condition (pollen or simple sugars).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from serial passage experiments.

claim: Negative interactions predominate in nutrient-rich environments.
source: This is consistent with previous observations that negative interactions predominate in nutrient-rich environments (Piccardi et al., 2019; Foster and Bell, 2012; Berry and Widder, 2014; Coyte et al., 2015; Ghoul and Mitri, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Piccardi et al., 2019; Foster and Bell, 2012; Berry and Widder, 2014; Coyte et al., 2015; Ghoul and Mitri, 2016).

claim: The four Lactobacillus species harbor relatively small genomes (1.5–2 Mb) with a conserved and streamlined core metabolism and similar auxotrophies.
source: Moreover, the four Lactobacillus species harbor relatively small genomes (1.5–2 Mb) with a conserved and streamlined core metabolism and similar auxotrophies, suggesting overlapping nutritional requirements (Ellegaard et al., 2019; Ellegaard et al., 2015; Kwong and Moran, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Ellegaard et al., 2019; Ellegaard et al., 2015; Kwong and Moran, 2016).

claim: The coexistence of the four Lactobacillus species in the honey bee gut primarily depends on the pollen diet of the host and not the host environment itself.
source: We thus conclude that the coexistence of the four Lactobacillus species in the honey bee gut primarily depends on the pollen diet of the host and not the host environment itself.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing stable coexistence in the presence of pollen both in vivo and in vitro.

claim: The nutritional conditions in vitro were sufficiently similar to recapitulate the overall community dynamics observed in vivo.
source: Although not identical, the nutritional conditions in vitro were sufficiently similar as to recapitulate the overall community dynamics observed in vivo: pollen nutrients supported the stable coexistence of the four species, while the simple sugars led to the dominance of a single species.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of in vivo and in vitro serial passage experiments showing similar patterns.

claim: Pollen nutrients supported the stable coexistence of the four species, while simple sugars led to the dominance of a single species.
source: Although not identical, the nutritional conditions in vitro were sufficiently similar as to recapitulate the overall community dynamics observed in vivo: pollen nutrients supported the stable coexistence of the four species, while the simple sugars led to the dominance of a single species.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from both in vivo and in vitro serial passage experiments.

claim: The findings are consistent with the consumer-resource model, which predicts that the number of species that can coexist depends on the number of available resources.

evidence: This claim is supported by citation to theoretical work (Tilman, 1986) and is consistent with the experimental results.

claim: In the presence of a single substrate, such as glucose in vitro, competition for the same nutrient results in the competitive exclusion of all but one species.
source: Correspondingly, in the presence of a single substrate, such as in the case of glucose in vitro, competition for the same nutrient results in the competitive exclusion of all but one species.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from in vitro serial passage experiments with glucose.

claim: Cross-feeding does not seem to play an important role in maintaining coexistence of the four Lactobacillus species.
source: However, cross-feeding does not seem to play an important role in maintaining coexistence of the four Lactobacillus species in this study.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the lack of evidence for cross-feeding in the metabolomics and transcriptomics data.

claim: Coexistence is facilitated by specialization toward distinct pollen-derived nutrients.
source: Instead, our combined transcriptomics and metabolomics analyses suggest that coexistence is facilitated by specialization toward distinct pollen-derived nutrients.

claim: All four species upregulated carbohydrate transport and metabolism functions dedicated to the utilization of different carbon sources in the presence of pollen when colonizing the bee gut.
source: We found that all four species upregulated carbohydrate transport and metabolism functions dedicated to the utilization of different carbon sources in the presence of pollen when colonizing the bee gut, and these changes were reproducible in vitro.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data from both in vivo and in vitro experiments.

claim: The metabolic specialization on plant glycans may be a common phenomenon in animal gut communities.
source: The metabolic specialization on plant glycans may be a common phenomenon in animal gut communities, as similar transcriptional changes have been described in other gut symbionts when the host diet was supplemented with specific plant glycans (Sonnenburg et al., 2005; Zheng et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is speculative and supported by citations to previous research (Sonnenburg et al., 2005; Zheng et al., 2019).

claim: Resource preference for at least one substrate is sufficient to explain coexistence.
source: While this may seem surprising, theoretical work has established that resource preference for at least one substrate is sufficient to explain coexistence (Meszéna et al., 2006).

claim: The four species utilize the same sugars, but extract them from different pollen-derived glycans.
source: Moreover, it is plausible that the four species utilize the same sugars, but extract them from different pollen-derived glycans, such as starch, hemicellulose, flavonoids, or other glycosylated secondary plant metabolites.

claim: Citrate co-fermentation has been linked to competitive advantages in lactic acid bacteria.
source: Citrate co-fermentation has been linked to competitive advantages in lactic acid bacteria, though whether the varying levels of co-fermentation contribute to colonization stability in this system remains an outstanding question (Laëtitia et al., 2014; Magni et al., 1999; Jimeno et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Laëtitia et al., 2014; Magni et al., 1999; Jimeno et al., 1995).

claim: The large diversity of carbohydrate transport and metabolism functions in the accessory gene pool of Lactobacillus Firm5 is an adaptation to the pollen-based diet of the host and a consequence of the nutrient competition with closely related species.
source: Previous work suggested that the large diversity of carbohydrate transport and metabolism functions in the accessory gene pool of Lactobacillus Firm5 is an adaptation to the pollen-based diet of the host and a consequence of the nutrient competition with closely related species (Ellegaard and Engel, 2019; Ellegaard et al., 2019).

claim: The findings provide the first experimental evidence for a link between the coexistence of the four Lactobacillus species, the large diversity of carbohydrate metabolism functions in their genomes, and the pollen diet of the host.
source: Our findings support this hypothesis and provide the first experimental evidence for a link between the coexistence of the four Lactobacillus species, the large diversity of carbohydrate metabolism functions in their genomes, and the pollen diet of the host.
evidence: This claim is supported by the combined experimental data from serial passage, transcriptomics, and metabolomics experiments.

source: Moreover, these results suggest that dietary differences between host species or natural variation in pollen diversity influence the diversity of Lactobacillus Firm5 and could, for example explain why the Asian honey bee, Apis cerana, harbors only one species of this phylotype in its gut (Ellegaard et al., 2020).

claim: Despite longstanding host association, gut bacterial interactions can be recapitulated in vitro providing insights about bacterial coexistence when combined with in vivo experiments.
